body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وصلى الله وسلم
أما بعد فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى هو الحكيم الخبير
وهذا الاستخلاف هو تشريف لهذا الجنس البشري وتكريم له، فقد كرم الله هذا الجنس بأنواع التكريم،
والاستخلاف في الأرض معناه أن كل ما في الأرض وهبه الله لهذا الجنس البشري، واستخلفه فيه
وهذا الاستخلاف يقتضي أن الإنسان خلق لحكمتين، إحداهما مختصة به وهي هذا الاستخلاف، فهي لهذا الجنس البشري وحده، لا يشركه فيها شيء من الخلائق، والحكمة الثانية مشتركة بين الإنس والجن وهي تحقيق العبادة لله.
قدر فيها أقواتها في أربعة أيام سواء للسائلين فكل ما في الأرض من الأرزاق قد كان خلق في ذلك الوقت، والناس يستغلونه مدة حياتهم ثم يتركونه لمن وراءهم ولا يصطحبون منه شيئا إلى قبورهم بل يتركونه
ومن هنا فلا بد أن يترك الإنسان بصماته في الأرض قبل موته، وأن يترك فيها آثارا حميدة فعمر الإنسان الحقيقي هو ما يخلفه وراءه من الآثار وما يتركه على ألسنة الناس من الثناء:
وإنما المرء حديث بعده ….
فيحتاج الإنسان إلى أن يكون له أثر في هذه الحياة، فالذي يولد ميلادا طبيعيا ويعيش حياة طبيعية ويموت موتا طبيعيا ولا يترك أثرا في الحياة الدنيا ينساه الناس، ولن يبقى له أثر في هذه الحياة، ولن يحقق المهمة التي من أجلها أهبط إلى الأرض، والإنسان غريب في هذه الأرض، جاء إليها وهو من بيئة أخرى بعيدة عنها، فقد أهبط أبونا آدم وأمنا حواء.
فهذه وظيفة حزب الله يسعون لإعلاء كلمة الله ونصرة دينه وهداية الناس، ووظيفة حزب الشيطان السعي لإغواء الناس وإضلالهم بتحقيق يمين إبليس بإغواء أكثر الناس، فقد أقسم على ذلك بعزة الله، كما حكى الله عنه:
وقد بين الله أن يمينه تحققت في أكثر البشر
فإذا كان يعلم أنه مصاب بداء عضال لا يمنعه ذلك من البناء والزرع والحرث لينتفع بذلك من يأتي بعده، وهكذا ولا يسعى للإفساد في الأرض، حتى ولو كان في ذلك الإفساد منفعة آنية مؤقتة له هو ولكن يترتب عليه الضرر في المستقبل فليس للإنسان أن يفعله، فالذي يبالغ مثلا في استعمال الماء ويسرف فيه لا يحقق الاستخلاف في الأرض لأنه يفسد ولو كان ذلك لمصلحة آنية مؤقتة له هو، فأهل الأرض يشكون شحا وندرة في المياه وسيزداد ذلك في الظروف المستقبلية، وكذلك فإن الذي يسرف في استغلال ما في الأرض من الخيرات والمناجم ونحوها أو حتى الأسماك التي في البحار إنما يضار الأجيال الآتية في أرزاقها، فعليه أن يأخذ بقدره وأن يكون عدلا في الأرض، حتى يكون استخلافه مؤديا لمهمته، ولذلك فإن إماطة الأذى عن الطريق صدقة وهي شعبة من شعب الإيمان، وكل ما فيه نفع عام فللإنسان فيه أجر كما ثبت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من حديث أنس بن مالك في صحيح مسلم أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ما من مسلم يغرز غرزا أو يزرع زرعا فيأكل منه طير أو يستظل به إنسان إلا كان له صدقة.
وكذلك فكل إصلاح في الأرض بالعدل والإنصاف هو من الاستخلاف،
وكذلك السعي لجمع قلوب المسلمين ولرأب الثأى بينهم ولتوحيد كلمتهم على الحق وللتقارب بين قلوبهم فكل ذلك من الاستخلاف الذي لا بد أن يحققه الإنسان في الأرض قبل أن ينصرف منها إلى الدار الآخرة، وكذلك فإن النفع العام مطلقا كالحفاظ على ممتلكات الدولة الإسلامية، والحفاظ على مصالح الشعوب ورعايتها وإحسان تمثيلها كل ذلك من الاستخلاف في الأرض.
وفي مقابله إهدار المال العام وإساءة استغلال المرافق العمومية كله من الإفساد في الأرض وهو مخالف للاستخلاف الذي ذكر، ونظير هذا ما يفعله كثير من الناس من إلقاء القمامات والأوساخ في الطرق ومن إساءة استغلال المرافق العمومية فكله مناف للاستخلاف في الأرض، فالاستخلاف في الأرض يقتضي من الإنسان أن لا يبول في الطريق وأن لا يلقي فيها قذرا ولا وسخا وأن يسعى لإماطة الأذى عن الطريق ما استطاع، وكذلك في استغلال المرافق العمومية على أحسن وجه، فإذا استغلها فهو يعلم أنها له ولمن سواه من أهله، فهو يأخذ بنصيبه ويتركها صالحة للاستعمال لمن يأتي وراءه، ومع الأسف فإن الناس يشاهدون أن كثيرا من الموظفين إذا تولوا وظيفة سعوا لاستغلالها
وهكذا في كل الأمور فلا بد من تحقيق الاستخلاف فيها، والحرص على أن يكون هذا الاستخلاف مقتضيا لأن يكون البشر استمرارا لهذا الجنس، فنحن الآن طبقة من طبقات البشر سبقنا كثير من الطبقات وإذا كان في الدنيا متسع فسيأتي بعدنا أيضا كثير من الطبقات، فنحن ورثنا آباءنا فيما في هذه الأرض من الخيرات، وسيرثنا أبناؤنا فينبغي أن نكون حلقة إيجابية تزيد ما كان موجودا من الخير ولا تنقصه، ولا تترك ميراثا صعبا للأجيال اللاحقة، ولذلك فإن كثيرا من الحكام والموظفين بمختلف مراتبهم ودرجاتهم يشكون من إرث من سبقهم، فكثير من الرؤساء يشكون من إرث من سبقهم فيكون السابق كان يتصرف على أنه آخر من يشغل هذه الوظيفة فيفسد فيها على ما يريد ويتصرف فيها تصرفا في غاية السوء، وهكذا كل من شغل وظيفة.
وإذا أدرك الإنسان استخلافه في الأرض وأنه يشغل الوظيفة مثل شغله لكرسي الحلاق يجلس عليه ليحلق رأسه ثم يقوم ليترك مكانه لغيره، وبقاؤه في أية وظيفة هو مثل بقاء جنازته على النعش ولا أحد يريد البقاء الدائم على كرسي الحلاق ولا أحد يريد البقاء الدائم على النعش، بل يحمل عليه فقط لمدة يسيرة كما قال الشاعر:
هو الموت ما منه ملاذ ومهرب والحكماء يقولون لو دامت لغيرك ما وصلت إليك
body_en:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, and may God's peace and blessings be upon

To proceed: God, Glorified and Exalted, is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.

This appointment as steward (istikhlāf) is an honour conferred upon the human kind and an ennobling of it, for God has honoured this kind with every sort of honouring,

and stewardship on the earth means that everything on the earth God has bestowed upon this human kind, and has appointed it steward over it.

This stewardship entails that the human being was created for two purposes. One of them belongs to him alone, and that is this stewardship: it is for the human kind by itself, and no other creature shares in it with him. The second purpose is shared between humankind and the jinn, and it is the realisation of the worship of God.

{and He determined therein its sustenance in four days, alike for those who ask} (Sūrat Fuṣṣilat 41:10). So everything on the earth of provision was created at that time; people make use of it for the span of their lives, then leave it to those who come after them, and take nothing of it with them to their graves — rather they leave it behind.

Hence a person must leave his imprint on the earth before his death, and must leave behind him praiseworthy traces. A person's true lifespan is what he leaves behind him of traces, and what he leaves on people's tongues of praise:

*A man is but a tale told after him ….*

So a person needs to have an effect in this life. One who is born a natural birth, lives a natural life and dies a natural death, and leaves no trace in the life of this world — people forget him, no trace of him will remain in this life, and he will not have fulfilled the task for which he was sent down to the earth. The human being is a stranger on this earth: he came to it from another realm far from it, for our father Adam and our mother Eve were sent down.

This, then, is the office of the party of God (ḥizb Allāh): they strive to raise high the word of God, to support His religion and to guide people. And the office of the party of Satan is to strive to seduce people and lead them astray, fulfilling the oath of Iblis to seduce most of mankind — for he swore to that by the might of God, as God has related of him:

And God has made clear that his oath was fulfilled in most of mankind

So even if he knows that he is afflicted with an incurable disease, that does not prevent him from building, planting and cultivating, so that whoever comes after him may benefit from it. And so too he does not strive to work corruption on the earth — even if in that corruption there is some immediate, temporary benefit for himself, but harm follows from it in the future, it is not for a person to do it. One who is excessive, for instance, in the use of water and wastes it does not fulfil stewardship on the earth, because he is working corruption, even if that is for an immediate, temporary interest of his own. The people of the earth complain of scarcity and want of water, and that will increase under future conditions. Likewise, one who is extravagant in exploiting what is in the earth of goods and mines and the like, or even the fish that are in the seas, harms the coming generations in their provision. He must take according to his measure and be just upon the earth, so that his stewardship discharges its task. For this reason the removal of harm from the road is a charity (ṣadaqah), and it is a branch among the branches of faith (īmān); and in everything in which there is general benefit there is reward for a person, as is established from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) in the hadith of Anas ibn Malik in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "There is no Muslim who sets a shoot in the ground or sows a crop, and then a bird eats of it or a human being takes shade by it, but that it is a charity for him."

And likewise every act of setting the earth right through justice and fairness is part of stewardship,

and likewise striving to gather the hearts of the Muslims, to mend the rift among them, to unite their word upon the truth, and to bring their hearts closer together — all of that is part of the stewardship that a person must fulfil on the earth before he departs from it to the abode of the Hereafter. And likewise general benefit without qualification, such as safeguarding the property of the Islamic state, and safeguarding the interests of the peoples, caring for them and representing them well — all of that is part of stewardship on the earth.

Over against it, the squandering of public money and the misuse of public utilities is all of it part of working corruption on the earth, and it is contrary to the stewardship that has been described. Comparable to this is what many people do in throwing rubbish and refuse in the roads and in misusing public utilities: all of it runs counter to stewardship on the earth. Stewardship on the earth requires of a person that he not urinate in the road, that he not cast filth or dirt into it, and that he strive to remove harm from the road as far as he is able; and likewise that he make use of public utilities in the best manner. When he uses them, he knows that they are his and also belong to others of his people besides him, so he takes his share and leaves them fit for use for whoever comes after him. Regrettably, people observe that many officials, when they take up a post, seek to exploit it

And so it is in all matters: stewardship must be fulfilled in them, with care that this stewardship entails that human beings be a continuation of this kind. We are now one layer among the layers of mankind: many layers preceded us, and if there is room left in this world, many layers will come after us as well. We inherited from our fathers what is on this earth of good things, and our children will inherit from us; so we ought to be a constructive link, which increases the good that was there and does not diminish it, and which does not leave a hard inheritance to the generations that follow. For this reason many rulers and officials, of every rank and degree, complain of the legacy of those who preceded them. Many heads of state complain of the legacy of those before them: the predecessor had behaved as though he were the last person ever to occupy that post, so he corrupted it as he pleased and dealt with it in the worst possible way. And so it is with everyone who has occupied a post.

And when a person grasps his stewardship on the earth, and that he occupies a post in the way that he occupies the barber's chair — he sits on it to have his head shaved, then rises to leave his place to another — and that his remaining in any post is like the remaining of his bier upon the litter; and no one wants to remain permanently on the barber's chair, and no one wants to remain permanently on the litter, but is carried on it only for a brief while, as the poet said:

*It is death: from it there is no refuge and no escape* — and the sages say: had it endured for another, it would never have reached you.

flags.arabic: كما حكى الله عنه:   /   وقد بين الله أن يمينه تحققت في أكثر البشر
flags.context: Two consecutive lines in the passage on the oath of Iblis; in the source each is followed immediately by unrelated prose, with no quotation in between.
options: Leave the lacunae visible, as done here
Restore the likely verses (Ṣād 38:82–83 and Sabaʾ 34:20) editorially
Withhold the page until the source is repaired
flags.note: The page drops the Qur'anic quotations the Sheikh introduced. 'as God has related of him:' is followed by nothing at all, and the statement that the oath was fulfilled is likewise left without its citation. Per house rule, the missing scripture has not been restored from memory. The passage is not readable as it stands and the source should be repaired before publication.

flags.arabic: قدر فيها أقواتها في أربعة أيام سواء للسائلين
flags.context: Appears bare, with no introduction and no quotation marking, at the head of a paragraph.
options: Mark as a Qur'anic quotation and supply the reference (as done here)
Leave it unmarked as the source does
flags.note: This is Qur'an 41:10, run into the surrounding prose without any marker in the source. It has been marked as a quotation and given its reference per house style, but the reader should know the marking is editorial, not present in the Arabic.

flags.context: A line of verse quoted in support of the point that a person's true lifespan is what he leaves behind.
options: Render only the surviving hemistich with its ellipsis, as done here
Complete the line from the well-known transmission
flags.note: The source gives only the first hemistich, followed by an ellipsis. The second hemistich has not been supplied, per the rule against restoring truncated quotations from memory.

flags.arabic: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وصلى الله وسلم
flags.context: The opening formula of the lecture.
options: Render the formula as it stands, incomplete
Complete it to the customary 'upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and Companions'
flags.note: The opening invocation breaks off: 'and may God's peace and blessings be upon' has no object in the Arabic. Left incomplete in the English, matching the source.

flags.context: فهذه وظيفة حزب الله يسعون لإعلاء كلمة الله ونصرة دينه وهداية الناس
options: the party of God (ḥizb Allāh) — the Qur'anic expression, contrasted with 'the party of Satan'
flags.note: Editorial care point for an English readership. The Sheikh is using the Qur'anic pair ḥizb Allāh / ḥizb al-shayṭān (Q 5:56, 58:19, 58:22) in its scriptural sense, and immediately contrasts it with 'the party of Satan'. It is in no way a reference to the Lebanese organisation, and must not be capitalised or transliterated in a way that suggests one.

flags.arabic: ومع الأسف فإن الناس يشاهدون أن كثيرا من الموظفين إذا تولوا وظيفة سعوا لاستغلالها
flags.context: End of the paragraph on the misuse of public utilities.
options: Treat the sentence as truncated in the source
flags.note: The sentence ends on 'seek to exploit it' with no object of exploitation and no closing punctuation, and the next paragraph starts a new topic. Consistent with the abridgement affecting the rest of the page. Rendered as it stands.

translator_notes: Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The published text is a heavily abridged transcript of a lecture. Several Qur'anic quotations that the Sheikh plainly recited have been dropped by whoever prepared the page, in two places leaving a colon or a clause with nothing after it. Those lacunae are left visible in the English exactly as they stand in the Arabic; nothing has been supplied. See the flags.
The text also breaks off at the end: the final 'and when a person grasps ...' clause never receives its main clause. The English ends where the Arabic ends.
